children: Restaurant stocks have come under pressure in 2026, with several major chains posting double-digit declines as investors assess slowing traffic trends, changing consumer spending habits and higher operating costs. According to industry data, McDonald's (MCD) is down about 18.7% year to date, while Yum Brands (YUM) has fallen roughly 9%. Domino's Pizza (DPZ) has been among the weakest performers, dropping more than 27% this year.

The sector's recent selloff has led investors to revisit valuations across leading restaurant operators, including Starbucks (SBUX), Restaurant Brands International (QSR), and Dutch Bros (BROS). Seeking Alpha noted that fundamentals vary widely despite the broad decline in restaurant shares.

Consumer demand remains uneven as customers focus more on value offerings and digital convenience. At the same time, operators continue to navigate labor inflation, commodity costs and promotional competition.

Performance has differed across the group. Starbucks shares are up about 15.6% year to date, while Restaurant Brands has gained nearly 10%, contrasting with declines at McDonald's, Yum Brands and Domino's.

Analysts cited in the report suggested the industry's outlook remains company-specific, with valuation, growth prospects and profitability likely to play a larger role than a broad sector recovery narrative.

title: Restaurant Stocks Are Tumbling. Here's Where Wall Street Sees Opportunity
